reconstruction_summary: Reconstructed agent's V3 generalising per-platform model (yp = shift(+1, k*(yp0 - b1))) using b1=0.000753865, k=1.068679, shift=+1 from out/results.json.
notes: Reconstructed V3 = shift(+1 sample, k*(yp0 - b1)) with b1=0.0007538650000000003, k=1.0686794838837996, shift=+1; parameters from out/results.json, fit on FORD_MUSTANG_MACH_E_MK1 only (agent excluded F-150 from their workspace). Applied identical Mustang-fit params across both Ford platforms in the canonical pool. baseline_rmse_recomputed (1.4740641e-02) matches the canonical baseline (1.4740021e-02) to ~6e-7; the small gap is because the +1-sample lag drops 449 segment-leading samples per pool (so our shared-mask baseline is over 1,364,476 samples vs canonical 1,364,925) -- this is not a recomputation discrepancy. 521 of 545 segments scored; 24 had all-NaN truth (mostly F-150 segments missing yaw_rate_meas_rads). agent_rmse > baseline_rmse: the Mustang-fit k=1.069 gain over-amplifies yaw on F-150 (and on segments outside the agent's train mask), so the per-platform calibration does not generalise to the pooled-Ford canonical set; the agent's own straight-regime regression warning (k>1 amplifies near-zero noise) compounds when applied across vehicles. Agent labels V4 (per-segment bias) as calibration not model improvement (rule 8); we score the V3 generalising model per their own headline declaration.
